name: Is tile a bad idea if my old kitchen floor keeps cracking or coming loose?

mainEntity.name: Is tile a bad idea if my old kitchen floor keeps cracking or coming loose?

acceptedAnswer.text: Tile is worth considering when you want a highly durable, water-resistant surface and are comfortable with a harder feel underfoot. It performs best over a properly prepared, stable, and sufficiently flat base with correctly planned joints and transitions. Context: Loose tiles and recurring grout failure can indicate movement, poor preparation, moisture, or an underlying base problem. The replacement scope should address that cause. Key factors: - Subfloor stability - Tile and grout maintenance - Slip resistance and texture - Added floor height Practical guidance: Ask how the installer will prepare the substrate and align tile height with adjoining rooms. Elite Remodeling & Design can incorporate tile selection into the broader kitchen layout and finish plan.
acceptedAnswer.description: Tile is not automatically a bad choice, but recurring cracks or loose pieces must be investigated first. Movement, moisture, poor leveling, or inadequate substrate preparation can cause the same failure again unless corrected.
